item.title: Still Here Fest - Beloved Asheville Benefit — Sat Sep 19, 7:00 PM — Fleetwood’s
item.description:
Still Here Fest is a celebration of the resilience of the Western North Carolina community. After the horrific events of Hurricane Helene, cities like Asheville and many others in the region saw firsthand the power and the strength of love and empathy. Spearheading the relief efforts, groups like Beloved Asheville and so many others dropped everything to serve, care for, and feed their community, neighbors, friends, and strangers alike. At the front of many of these relief efforts were the artists and musicians, putting aside their creative drive to take time to bring food, water, and other life-saving supplies to those in need. Still Here Fest 2026 is in recognition of not only the efforts of these groups and individuals but also the resilient spirit of Western North Carolina. We survive, we thrive, we are still here.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: The Southern Highland Craft Guild's 46th Annual Heritage Weekend — Sun Sep 20, 10:00 AM — Folk Art Center
item.description:
You are invited to our 46th. annual Heritage Weekend on September 19 and 20 at the Folk Art Center on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Many of you have been to this fun event in the past and we will again host over 20 heritage artist, musicians and dancers to honor and celebrate Mountain Heritage Crafts. One of the highlights of the celebration is our Annual World Gee Haw Whimmy Diddle competition on Saturday afternoon. A Whimmy Diddle is an Appalachian mountain toy, traditionally made from 2 sticks of rhododendron. Notches are carved into the stick and a propeller is attached to the end. Rubbing the notches with the second stick makes the propeller spin! The trick is to make it spin gee (to the right) or haw (to the left). Contestants are judged by their skills and interesting prizes will be awarded. The music stage will provide entertainment with Blue Grass and Gospel music, and cloggers will demonstrate the mountain dance tradition.

item.title: Craven Gap Out-and-Back -- 5 mi, 800 ft. elev. gain — Fri Sep 25, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Sign ups open Sunday, Sept. 20th, 8:00 PM]**
This segment of the Mountain-to-Sea Trail was devastated by Hurricane Helene and closed for well over a year. But now it's back! If you're familiar with this hike, the first mile was radically altered. After that, it looks a little more "normal."
From the Craven Gap parking lot, we cross the Parkway and head south on the Mountain-to-Sea Trail. It's hilly but doesn't add up to much elevation gain. We'll take a short break 2.5 miles out, then return the way we came. It's more scenic than in the past due to lots of new vistas that used to be blocked by trees. Otherwise, just your basic, beautiful, winding forest trail. At our pace (about 2.4 mph), I'd give it a 3.5/10 difficulty rating. We should be back in the parking lot soon after noon.
Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but Forestry Service regulations require leashes.

item.title: Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons — Sat Oct 10, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons with Carlton Burke Satuday, October 10 | 12 – 4pm BRN – Core Register Here!
Since birds are capable of long distance flights and many engage in annual migration rituals, their presence in our area often changes in relation to the seasons of the year. In this class we will discuss the seasonal patterns of southern Appalachian birds and focus on some of the major species and their annual life cycles. As part of this program, there will be a “lab” portion where students will be able to meet some live birds and participate in other hands-on components to deepen the learning. Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. We will be using Newcomb’s guide to key out some of the less common flowers but will focus on learning how to look closely at flowers to identify them. item.description: This workshop will give you hands-on experience working with several pulps to learn the basics of western style mould and deckle papermaking. You will learn: • how to process recycled and commercial fibers into pulp at home or in a paper studio • what tools and equipment are needed for papermaking • how to pull, press and dry sheets of paper The day will start with a discussion about papermaking and will explore a variety of handmade paper samples. Afterwards, we will set up vats of pulp and make sheets of paper together. Each participant will take home a stack of sample papers. It’s up to you how you use the finished sheets. All are welcome. No experience necessary. Alyssa Sacora (she/her) is a crafts person working in plant-based mediums of papermaking, book arts, basketry, and weaving.
